name: 50 Cold Email Templates That Get Replies
description: 50 proven cold email templates for every situation. B2B sales, partnerships, job applications, networking, and more. Each template includes psychology notes and personalization tips.

templates.name: The Pattern Interrupt
templates.subject: Quick question, {{firstName}}
templates.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

I know you get 100 cold emails a day, so I'll be brief.

{{company}} is doing something interesting with {{specificObservation}}. We helped {{similarCompany}} go from {{beforeMetric}} to {{afterMetric}} in {{timeframe}} by {{method}}.

Worth a 10-minute chat next week?

{{senderName}}
templates.psychology: Acknowledges email overload (empathy), shows research (not generic), provides proof with similar company (social proof), low-friction ask (10 min).
templates.personalization: Replace {{specificObservation}} with something genuinely specific you noticed about their company.

templates.name: The Value-First Approach
templates.subject: I analyzed {{company}}'s {{specificArea}}
templates.psychology: Delivers value before asking for anything. Creates reciprocity. Shows expertise without bragging.
templates.personalization: Actually do the analysis. This only works if the findings are genuine and specific.

templates.name: The Social Proof Hammer
templates.subject: {{mutualConnection}} suggested we connect
templates.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

{{mutualConnection}} mentioned you're the person to talk to about {{topic}} at {{company}}.

We recently helped {{clientName}} {{specificResult}} — they were dealing with {{specificPainPoint}}, which sounds similar to what {{company}} might be facing.

Open to a quick intro call?

{{senderName}}

P.S. {{mutualConnection}} said to say hello!
templates.psychology: Referral creates instant trust. Social proof with named client. P.S. reinforces the connection.
templates.personalization: Only use if you actually have a mutual connection who gave you permission.

templates.name: The Problem-Agitate-Solve
templates.subject: {{painPoint}} at {{company}}?
templates.psychology: PAS framework. Agitates the pain before presenting the solution. Calendar link reduces friction.
templates.personalization: The pain point must be specific enough that they feel 'how did you know?'

templates.name: The Case Study Drop
templates.subject: How {{clientName}} {{achievedResult}}
templates.psychology: Provides free value (case study). 'No pitch' reduces resistance. Ends with soft CTA.
templates.personalization: Pick a case study that's relevant to their industry or challenge.

templates.name: The Win-Win Pitch
templates.subject: Partnership idea: {{yourCompany}} + {{company}}
templates.psychology: Shows research. Frames as win-win. Specific enough to be actionable but open enough to invite collaboration.
templates.personalization: Propose a specific partnership model, not just 'let's partner.'

templates.name: The Co-Marketing Proposal
templates.subject: Idea: {{company}} + {{yourCompany}} content collab
templates.psychology: Concrete proposal with clear division of labor. Shows you've thought it through. Mutual benefit is obvious.
templates.personalization: Propose a content type that matches their brand voice.

templates.name: The Hiring Manager Direct
templates.subject: {{role}} position — {{yourName}}
templates.psychology: Bypasses ATS by going direct. Leads with quantified achievements. Shows initiative. Easy to scan.
templates.personalization: Research the hiring manager's name on LinkedIn. Reference a specific team or project they own.

templates.name: The Informational Interview
templates.subject: Quick question about your work at {{company}}
templates.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

I'm a {{yourRole}} interested in transitioning into {{targetField}}. Your career path from {{theirPreviousRole}} to {{theirCurrentRole}} at {{company}} is exactly what I aspire to.

Would you be open to a 15-minute coffee chat (virtual or in-person)? I'd love to hear about:
• Your experience at {{company}}
• What you wish you'd known starting out
• Any advice for someone making this transition

No agenda — genuinely just looking to learn.

{{senderName}}
templates.psychology: Flatters genuinely. Low ask (15 min). 'No agenda' reduces resistance. People love helping those who admire them.
templates.personalization: Reference something specific about their career path that you genuinely admire.

templates.name: The Value-Add Networking Message
templates.subject: Thought you'd find this useful, {{firstName}}
templates.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

I read your {{content type — post/article/talk}} about {{topic}}. Really insightful take on {{specificPoint}}.

It reminded me of {{relevantResource}} — thought you might find it useful for your work at {{company}}.

No response needed — just wanted to share.

If you're ever open to connecting, I'd love to learn more about {{theirWork}}.

{{senderName}}
templates.psychology: Leads with value (a resource). 'No response needed' removes pressure. Creates the opening for a relationship.
templates.personalization: The resource must genuinely be relevant. Don't force it.

templates.name: The Gentle Bump (3 days)
templates.subject: Re: {{originalSubject}}
templates.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

Floating this to the top of your inbox in case it got buried.

No rush — just wanted to make sure you saw my note about {{topic}}.

{{senderName}}
templates.psychology: Acknowledges they're busy. Low guilt. Short and friendly.

templates.name: The Value Add (7 days)
templates.subject: Re: {{originalSubject}} — thought of something
templates.psychology: New reason to engage. Doesn't guilt-trip. Provides additional value.
templates.personalization: The value-add should be different from your original email.

templates.name: The Breakup Email (14 days)
templates.subject: Closing the loop
templates.psychology: Creates FOMO. Removes you from their inbox. Often triggers replies from people who meant to respond but forgot.
templates.personalization: Be genuinely warm. You may cross paths again.

templates.name: The Different Angle (21 days)
templates.subject: Different approach: {{newAngle}}
templates.psychology: Shows persistence without being annoying. Demonstrates you're thinking, not just spamming. New angle = new reason to engage.
templates.personalization: The new angle must be genuinely different, not a rephrasing.

templates.name: The Mentor Ask
templates.subject: Seeking guidance from someone who's been there
templates.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

I've been following your work at {{company}} for a while — particularly {{specificWork}}. Your trajectory from {{theirBackground}} to {{currentRole}} is exactly the path I'm working toward.

I'm currently {{yourSituation}} and could really use advice from someone who's navigated this stage.

Would you be willing to be an informal mentor? Just a 30-minute call once a quarter. I'll come prepared with specific questions and won't waste your time.

{{senderName}}
templates.psychology: Specific and respectful. Low commitment (quarterly). Shows you'll value their time. Flattering without being sycophantic.
templates.personalization: Reference specific work they've done — show you're not mass-emailing.

templates.name: The Investor Update
templates.subject: {{company}} update — {{metric}}
templates.psychology: Scannable format. Leads with numbers. Clear ask. Not asking for money directly — keeping them in the loop.
templates.personalization: Only send to investors or potential investors who've shown interest.

templates.name: The We Miss You
templates.subject: We miss you at {{company}}, {{firstName}}
templates.psychology: Shows what they missed. Incentive to return. Personal accountability for past issues.
templates.personalization: The updates should be relevant to why they might have left.

templates.name: The Check-In (No Pitch)
templates.subject: How are things going, {{firstName}}?
templates.body:
Hi {{firstName}},

Not reaching out to sell you anything — just wanted to check in.

Last time we talked, you were working on {{specificProject}}. How did that turn out?

If there's anything I can help with — even if it's not related to {{product}} — let me know.

{{senderName}}
templates.psychology: Zero pitch. Genuinely human. Often reopens conversations naturally.
templates.personalization: Reference a specific detail from your last conversation.
